name: Brand Master Academy
shortDescription: Long interviews with the people who actually do brand positioning for a living, on the process rather than the aesthetics.
longDescription: The substantial material here is a set of thirty-nine to sixty-three minute conversations with practitioners whose work is positioning rather than visual identity — April Dunford on why most business-to-business positioning fails, Bobby Moesta on how buyers actually change their minds, Blair Enns on selling expertise, Laura Ries on why a brand needs an opponent. That roster is the reason for the listing: these are people with a method and a track record rather than commentators. A repositioning case study on milk is the clearest demonstration of what the discipline consists of when it is done properly. The channel's own material — three-pillar frameworks, positioning triggers — is thinner and more formulaic than the interviews. Note the shape: forty-two of the fifty most recent uploads are under two minutes, so the interviews are a small fraction of what you will first see.
notFor: Anyone looking for logo, identity or visual design work — this is positioning and strategy, and the visual layer is barely touched. It also assumes you are advising clients or running a business, not building a personal brand.

categories.why: Deciding what to stand for in a customer's mind, treated as a process with steps and named practitioners rather than as taste — and with the failure modes discussed as often as the successes.
categories.evidence: Forty-six minutes with April Dunford on why business-to-business positioning fails, fifty-three with Bobby Moesta on how buyers change their minds, a thirty-six-minute repositioning case study on milk, and fifty minutes on agency strategy processes with Bill Kenney.

entryVideo.title: Why Most B2B Positioning Fails with April Dunford
entryVideo.whyThisOne: Starts from the failure rather than the framework, with the practitioner most associated with getting positioning right — which makes the frameworks elsewhere on the channel easier to judge.

caveats: A course business with heavy funnelling — the channel exists to sell a brand-strategy programme and the short-form content is built for that. The interviews are the substance; the in-house framework videos are the pitch. Guests are frequently promoting their own books.
